questions.question_text: What are the first four terms of the sequence defined by $a_{n} = 4n - 1$?

options.why: Multiplied by 4 without subtracting 1 for each term.
Substituted $n = 0, 1, 2, 3$ instead of starting at $n = 1$.
Added 1 to the first term instead of applying the formula $4n-1$.

questions.question_text:
A sequence is defined recursively by $a_{1} = 4$ and $a_{n} = 3a_{n-1} - 5$ for $n \ge 2$.
What is the value of $a_{3}$?

options.why: Found the second term $a_{2}$ instead of the third term $a_{3}$.
Calculated $a_{4}$ instead of $a_{3}$ by applying the recurrence three times.
Substituted $n = 3$ into $3n - 5$ instead of using the recursive rule.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the sequence $5, 10, 15, 20, \dots, 105$?

options.text: It is a finite sequence because it terminates at the 21st term, $105$.
It is an infinite sequence because the terms increase by 5 each time without bound.
options.why: Ignored the terminating last term 105 in the given list.

options.text: It is an infinite sequence because ellipsis dots always represent an infinite list.
options.why: Assumed ellipsis always denotes an infinite sequence even with a final term.

options.text: It is a finite sequence with exactly 105 terms.
options.why: Confused the value of the last term 105 with the total number of terms.

questions.solution_text:
The sequence has a specified final term $105$.
Therefore, it is a finite sequence.

questions.question_text: For the sequence $a_{n} = 9n - 4$, what is the position number $n$ of the term whose value is $113$?

options.why: Gave the term value instead of its position number.
Subtracted 4 from 113 instead of adding 4 before dividing by 9.
Calculated $a_{113} = 9(113) - 4$ instead of solving for $n$.

questions.question_text: Determine whether $88$ is a term of the sequence given by $a_{n} = 7n + 5$.

options.text: No, because solving $7n + 5 = 88$ gives $n = \frac{83}{7}$, which is not an integer.
Yes, it is the 12th term because $\frac{83}{7}$ rounds up to 12.
options.why: Rounded a non-integer position number to the nearest integer.

options.text: Yes, because $88$ is an even number greater than $a_{1} = 12$.
options.why: Judged term membership by parity and magnitude instead of solving for $n$.

options.text: No, because $88 - 5 = 83$ is not divisible by 5.
options.why: Checked divisibility by 5 instead of the coefficient 7.

questions.solution_text:
$7n + 5 = 88$
$7n = 83$
$n = \dfrac{83}{7} \approx 11.857$
Since $n$ is not an integer, $88$ is not a term of the sequence.

questions.question_text: How many negative terms are in the sequence $a_{n} = 8n - 95$?

options.why: Rounded $11.875$ up to 12 instead of taking integers strictly less than $11.875$.
Subtracted an extra term after solving the inequality.
Subtracted 8 from 95 instead of solving $8n < 95$.

questions.solution_text:
$8n - 95 < 0$
$8n < 95$
$n < 11.875$
The positive integer indices are $n = 1, 2, \dots, 11$.
There are $11$ negative terms.

options.why: Gave the position number $n=9$ instead of the term value $a_{9} = 4$.
Calculated the 8th term $a_{8} = -2$, which is not greater than 0.
Used $n = 10$ instead of the smallest integer index $n = 9$.

questions.question_text: Determine whether $324$ is a term of the sequence $a_{n} = 4n^{2}$.

options.text: Yes, it is the 9th term ($a_{9}$).
Yes, it is the 81st term ($a_{81}$).
options.why: Found $n^{2} = 81$ and forgot to take the square root to find $n$.

options.text: No, because $324$ is not divisible by 16.
options.why: Divided by $4^{2} = 16$ instead of dividing by the coefficient 4.

options.text: Yes, it is both the 9th and $-9$th term.
options.why: Included the negative root $n = -9$, which is not a valid position number.

questions.solution_text:
$4n^{2} = 324$
$n^{2} = 81$
$n = 9$
Since $n = 9$ is a positive integer, $324$ is the 9th term ($a_{9}$).

questions.question_text: Find the 5th term of the sequence defined by $a_{n} = (-1)^{n+1} \cdot \dfrac{n^{2}}{n+3}$.

options.why: Evaluated $(-1)^{5+1}$ as $-1$ instead of $+1$.
Substituted $n = 4$ instead of $n = 5$.
